record.paper_title: Optimal scaling of average queue sizes in an input-queued switch: an open problem
record.original_question: In the same n by n input-queued switch model with load factor ρ(λ) and optimal steady-state expected total queue size Q*(n,λ), what is β*_2, the infimum over positive β for which there is a constant c > 0 such that, for every arrival-rate matrix λ with ρ(λ) < 1, the limit superior as n approaches infinity of Q*(n,λ)/n^β is at most c/(1 − ρ(λ))? Is this exponent equal to 1?

evidence.quote: Find β∗2, the infimum over all positive numbers β for which there exists a constant c > 0 such that lim sup n→∞ 1/nβ · Q∗(n,λ) ≤ c/(1 − ρ(λ)).
We conjecture that β∗0 = 1, which would also imply that β∗1 = 1 and β∗2 = 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time n×n input-queued switch. At each input port i ∈ {1,…,n} and output port j ∈ {1,…,n}, there is a queue Q_{ij} storing packets that arrive at input i destined for output j. In each time slot, packets arrive at input i destined for output j according to independent Bernoulli processes with rate λ_{ij} ≥ 0, where λ = (λ_{ij}) is a nonnegative arrival-rate matrix satisfying the admissibility constraint

ρ(λ) := max{ max_i Σ_j λ_{ij}, max_j Σ_i λ_{ij} } < 1.

In each time slot the scheduler selects a matching (a permutation) σ of {1,…,n} and serves one packet from each nonempty queue Q_{i,σ(i)}. A scheduling policy is any (online, causal) rule choosing σ in each time slot. For a stable policy, let Q^π(n,λ) denote the steady-state expected total queue size E[Σ_{i,j} Q_{ij}] under policy π. Define

Q*(n,λ) := inf_π Q^π(n,λ),

the infimum taken over all (online) scheduling policies under which the system is positive recurrent.

Define β*_2 to be the infimum over all positive real numbers β for which there exists a constant c > 0 such that, for every admissible arrival-rate matrix λ with ρ(λ) < 1,

limsup_{n → ∞} Q*(n,λ) / n^β ≤ c / (1 − ρ(λ)).

Determine β*_2. In particular, is β*_2 = 1?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the optimal scaling is Θ(n/(1−ρ)) (which would give β*_2 = 1) remains the standing open problem. Partial progress exists: Shah–Walton–Zhong (Ann. Appl. Probab., 2014) established optimal n/(1−ρ) scaling in the heavy-traffic regime 1−ρ = O(1/n²); later work (e.g., improved scaling via graph factorization) yields bounds such as O(n^{1.5} log(1/(1−ρ))/(1−ρ)) in the regime 1−ρ = O(1/n), improving prior O(n³) bounds. No full resolution showing β*_2 = 1 appears to have been published as of the search.

status_evidence.title: Optimal queue-size scaling in switched networks
status_evidence.snippet: Shah, Walton, Zhong establish optimal Θ(n/(1−ρ)) queue-size scaling in the regime 1−ρ = O(1/n²).
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture verified in a restricted heavy-traffic regime.

status_evidence.title: On Queue-Size Scaling for Input-Queued Switches
status_evidence.snippet: Provides improved scaling bounds for input-queued switches beyond the heavy traffic regime.
status_evidence.claim: Partial improvements but conjecture not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Improved queue-size scaling for input-queued switches via graph factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Improved bounds on Q*(n,λ) using graph factorization techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Further progress on bounds, full conjecture remains open.
